# vk v0.3.0

Date: 2026-10-25. Status: Experimental development release.
Cargo package: `vkrust`. Rust library/import: `vk`. License: MIT.

## Scope

This first public development release combines the native allocator checkpoints
since v0.2.3 with a public-source, CI and package-publication pipeline. All 842
command spellings in the pinned Vulkan registry have callable operations,
including core Vulkan 1.0–1.4. This is pinned callable coverage, not Vulkan
conformance or production qualification.

The public and private release lanes share version `0.3.0` and tag `v0.3.0`.
Public commits contain sanitized source without private history, internal
engineering documents or editor/agent configuration. Their Git commit IDs
therefore differ from private release commits. The snapshot marker records the
exact private source commit.

## Changes

- Publish original code and Cargo license metadata under MIT; preserve Khronos
  provenance and upstream AMD MIT attribution for derived allocator algorithms.
- Harden dedicated allocations with admitted requirements2/dedication chains,
  queried size ceilings, explicit resource cleanup and failure-safe ownership.
- Add opt-in homogeneous pooled buffers with TLSF placement, shared explicit
  and persistent mapping, non-coherent atom isolation and checked cache ranges.
- Add native Rust host-only virtual placement, donor strategies, checked tokens
  and statistics. Drop still performs no native cleanup or implicit completion.
- Add pinned VMA differential oracles, independent interval/lifecycle models,
  host-allocation failure injection and native compute/readback profiles.
- Add public-only CI for generation, strict Rust gates, independent ABI/PFN and
  feature oracles, Windows/macOS host tests and explicit Lavapipe workloads.
- Verify a real Cargo archive, its test inputs and independent consumers with
  minimal, loader and allocator features. Keep the generator unpublished.
- Stage the verified crate, Rust API reference, checksums and build evidence as
  GitHub release assets. Optional crates.io publication compares exact archive
  bytes and verifies the downloaded registry artifact. API docs use docs.rs.

## Compatibility

Use `vk = { package = "vkrust", version = "0.3" }`. Rust 1.98.1 and edition 2024
are the declared baseline. Optional memory APIs remain experimental; enable
`allocator` explicitly. Default buffer storage remains separate, with pooled
storage selected by policy. Pooled allocations can share native memory and
have nonzero binding offsets. Cleanup must occur explicitly after completion.

## Verification and limitations

The release is gated on host tests, deterministic generation, package-consumer
execution, warnings-denied lint/docs and pinned-header layout/prototype and
feature checks. Hosted CI results, when available, are the evidence for the
configured runner matrix; declaring jobs does not qualify their targets.
Lavapipe correctness is distinct from physical GPU qualification.

The recorded physical profile remains x86-64 Linux, Intel HD Graphics 4400
(Haswell), Vulkan 1.2 and Mesa. Vulkan 1.3/1.4 physical execution, WSI,
positive video/ray-tracing, external interop and protected-platform C ABI
qualification remain open. The allocator is not VMA-equivalent. No universal
safety, performance or production-readiness claim is made. See
[qualification and limitations](../qualification.md).

A GitHub release does not imply crates.io publication. The latter additionally
requires registry authentication and a successful publication/byte-verification
job. An unpublished name is not reserved by creating a Git tag.
